solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Bird continues to nest in hide (6)

indicatorNotes.to nest in: one piece settles inside another like an egg in a nest

blocks.note: a hide is an animal's skin
to be is to continue existing

annotation.surface: A birdwatcher's note that some bird keeps nesting near the hide.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like the birdwatcher's shelter from the surface; here it is an animal's skin.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the siskin is a small finch.

entries.clue: Pains in rear from nasty infection for the duration of the game (8)

indicatorNotes.in rear: the rear of a word is its last letter, so take that

blocks.note: all day = for the duration of the day

annotation.surface: Someone suffers a sore backside from an infection throughout a match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pains in rear' reads as one complaint, but it is an instruction: take the rear of 'pains'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: softball is one game, a larger-balled cousin of baseball.

entries.clue: All but crack the central character in Peter Pan (7)

indicatorNotes.All but: all but = nearly all, so everything except the last letter
indicatorNotes.the central character in: a character is a letter, and the central one is the middle letter

blocks.note: crack = SKILLED (a crack shot), without its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone is cracking up about the hero of Peter Pan.
annotation.walkthrough: Peter Pan is split: Peter supplies a letter and Pan is the definition. 'Crack' is the adjective, as in crack troops.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a skillet is a frying pan.

entries.clue: Possibly lying at home, seeing what’s before me (9)

blocks.note: in do-re-mi, re comes before mi

annotation.surface: Someone lounging at home watches whatever is in front of them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Me' is the note mi in the sol-fa scale. 'Lying' looks like lounging but means telling untruths.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone insincere is not speaking truthfully, so may well be lying; 'possibly' covers the looseness.

entries.clue: Swiss produce soldiers to probe meat supply line (8)

indicatorNotes.to probe: a probe pushes into something, so one piece pushes into another
indicatorNotes.supply: read as 'supplely': the letters are bent into a new shape

annotation.surface: Swiss troops are sent to inspect a meat supply route.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is the adverb of supple, not the noun it poses as, and 'supply line' is a false phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Emmental is a cheese made in Switzerland, so one piece of Swiss produce.

entries.clue: Notice several days in Spring fitting around Golf Society (8,6)

indicatorNotes.around: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: part of March falls in spring
in order = fitting, proper; wrapped around G
G = golf in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A notice about several spring days suits the golf club.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Notice' reads as a posted announcement, but it is being given notice: sacked.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to get your marching orders is to be dismissed, which is being given notice.

entries.clue: Be disparaging about women perhaps going topless (5)

indicatorNotes.going topless: in a down clue the top is the first letter, and topless loses it

annotation.surface: Someone is sneering at women who go topless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Be' looks like the start of an instruction ('be disparaging') but it stands alone as the definition. 'Perhaps' allows that sexism need not target women.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to be, in the philosophical sense, is to exist.

entries.clue: Part of Rashid’s armoury steals trophy from the ground (7)

indicatorNotes.from the ground: in a down clue, starting from the ground means reading upward from the bottom

blocks.note: a pot is a cup or trophy

annotation.surface: A thief takes a trophy out of someone's arsenal at a sports ground.
annotation.walkthrough: Adil Rashid is an England leg-spin bowler in cricket; the surface makes his armoury sound like weapons.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: topspin is a spinner's variation, one item in Rashid's bowling armoury.

entries.clue: Down south in remote lands (6)

indicatorNotes.Down south: south is S, and in a down clue sending it down moves it to the bottom

blocks.note: the S at the top moves to the foot of the column

annotation.surface: Somewhere far down in the southern lands.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Down south' sounds like a place; here it is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to light on something is to land or alight on it.

entries.clue: I’m relaxed about that light approach and effort? (4,4,4,2)

blocks.note: have a go = make an effort

annotation.surface: Someone claims to be unbothered by a gentle approach and a bit of effort.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Light' governs both nouns, so 'and' brings it back a second time.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: the saying shrugs off a loss, the voice of someone relaxed about it.

entries.clue: It’s just beginning to sell in markets (5,4)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.in: in places that letter inside the other piece

annotation.surface: A trader is just starting to sell at markets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Just' pretends to mean 'only', but it means fair.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'fair's fair' is said to insist that something is only just.

entries.clue: Periodic suppression of kidnapping and — imminently — dropping litter (2,3)

indicatorNotes.Periodic suppression of: periodic means at regular intervals, so every other letter is suppressed

blocks.note: kIdNaPpInG: the odd letters are suppressed

annotation.surface: A report on regular clampdowns on kidnapping and on dropping litter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like rubbish, but it is a sow's piglets.
annotation.definitionFit: Farming idiom: a sow in pig is pregnant, so imminently she will drop a litter.

entries.clue: Heartless lad grabs single bunk (7)

indicatorNotes.Heartless: the heart of a word is its middle, and heartless removes it
indicatorNotes.grabs: to grab is to hold, so the outer piece holds another inside

blocks.note: BOY with its middle O removed

annotation.surface: A cold-hearted boy seizes a bed in a dormitory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' looks like a bed; it is nonsense.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: bunk (from bunkum) and baloney both mean nonsense.

entries.clue: Warning from Spooner in the kitchen, where there’s great activity (7)

indicatorNotes.from Spooner: Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: a warning cried at the stove, with the first sounds swapped
surface padding that places the warning at the stove

annotation.surface: Spooner calls out a warning in a busy kitchen.
annotation.walkthrough: The kitchen warning is 'Pot's hot!'; 'in the kitchen' just sets the scene for it.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a hotspot is a place of intense activity.

entries.clue: Rich, released from Further Education, revolutionised capacity (5)

indicatorNotes.released from: letters released from a word leave it
indicatorNotes.revolutionised: a revolution overturns order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: FE = further education, removed to leave RTILE

annotation.surface: A wealthy man, freed from college, transformed his abilities.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rich' looks like a person or wealth; it is fertile, as rich soil is. FE is British further education, post-school college.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the litre is one unit of capacity.

entries.clue: Medication program overlooked by office (8)

indicatorNotes.overlooked by: what is overlooked is ignored, so the program is left out of the office word

blocks.note: an office is an appointment, a post
an app is a computer program; it is omitted

annotation.surface: A medication scheme is ignored by head office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Overlooked' means ignored here, not looked down on.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: ointment is medication rubbed on the skin.

entries.clue: Looking to heaven, this writer’s inspiring leporine sage (9)

indicatorNotes.Looking to heaven: heaven is up, so in a down clue the letters read upward
indicatorNotes.inspiring: to inspire is to breathe in, so the outer piece takes another inside

annotation.surface: An upturned writer is gripped by a hare-like wise man.
annotation.walkthrough: Leporine means like a hare; the setter spells hare-ish as HARISH, a joke spelling.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a maharishi is a Hindu sage or spiritual teacher.

entries.clue: Plant joint tenants outside of town (4,4)

indicatorNotes.tenants: to tenant a place is to occupy it, so the joint lives inside the outer letters of town

blocks.note: a joint is a cannabis cigarette, a reefer

annotation.surface: Joint tenants take a place on the edge of town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joint tenants' is a legal phrase; split it, and 'tenants' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a tree fern is a fern that grows a tall trunk.

entries.clue: One for the road? This may stop me indulging (8)

blocks.note: a final drink before leaving, read as three words: drink before leaving

annotation.surface: A drinker offered a last one wonders whether conscience will stop them.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: split as SUP ERE GO it is 'drink before leaving', which is what one for the road is.
annotation.definitionFit: In Freud, the superego is the conscience that restrains the ego, me, from indulging; the whimsical first sense is sup ere go.

entries.clue: Carrying very minute drops from impure liquid, runs towards source (7)

indicatorNotes.Carrying: to carry something is to hold it, so the outer piece holds V
indicatorNotes.drops from: what drops from a word leaves it, so the M goes
indicatorNotes.liquid: liquid flows into any shape, so the remaining letters rearrange

blocks.note: M = minute, dropped to leave IPURE, rearranged UPRIE

annotation.surface: A chemist notes that dirty liquid, carried in tiny drops, runs back to its origin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Liquid' looks like the noun of the surface; it is the adjective meaning fluid.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: upriver means towards the river's source.

entries.clue: One on the wing that races linesman (5)

annotation.definition: One on the wing that races

blocks.clueFragment: One on the wing that races
blocks.note: a homing pigeon, bred for racing
the Greek epic poet, a man of lines of verse

annotation.surface: A winger who outruns the linesman on a football pitch.
annotation.walkthrough: The football picture hides both senses: a winger is a bird on the wing, and the linesman writes lines of verse.
annotation.definitionFit: Double definition: a homer is a racing pigeon, and Homer wrote lines of epic verse.

entries.clue: Not much covering one ousting Democrat from US (7)

indicatorNotes.ousting: to oust is to push out and take the place of, so one letter replaces another

blocks.note: D = Democrat, the letter pushed out

annotation.surface: A report on something small, about an official ousting a Democrat in America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'US' looks like the United States but is the pronoun: us, mankind.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a mankini is a skimpy men's swimsuit, hardly any covering.

entries.clue: Up to carrying cross? It’ll repel evil (6)

indicatorNotes.carrying: to carry something is to hold it, so the outer piece holds another

blocks.note: 'what are you at?' = what are you up to?
a mule is a cross between horse and donkey

annotation.surface: Someone is ready to bear a crucifix to keep evil away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a crucifix, which fits the evil-repelling surface; here it is a hybrid animal.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: an amulet is a charm worn to ward off evil.

entries.clue: Warring figure after some liquor (7)

blocks.note: à la = after the manner of

annotation.surface: A combatant goes looking for a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' is not order here but à la, in the style of.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Marsala is a fortified Sicilian wine, so some liquor.

entries.clue: Vessel that road carries north (5)

indicatorNotes.carries: the phrase carries the letters inside it
indicatorNotes.north: north is up, so in a down clue the letters read upward

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words: thAT ROAd

annotation.surface: A ship is carried north along a road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' looks like a boat; it is a blood vessel.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the aorta is the body's main artery, a blood vessel.

entries.clue: Don’s neighbour has called in disarray (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'has called in' puts the calling inside the river

blocks.note: the Dee and the Don are neighbouring rivers at Aberdeen

annotation.surface: A neighbouring academic has phoned in a muddle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university teacher; it is a Scottish river. 'Disarray' is a verb: to throw into disorder.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both verbs: to derange something is to throw it out of order.

entries.clue: Organ donor has left for good (5)

indicatorNotes.for: for = in place of, so L goes in the place of G

annotation.surface: An organ donor has died.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left for good' reads as gone forever; split it, and it is a letter swap.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the liver is one organ, and one a living donor can part-give.

entries.clue: In the old days, duck cycled around historic county (9)

indicatorNotes.cycled: cycling a word moves its last letter round to the front
indicatorNotes.around: around means surrounding, so the outer piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to duck a duty is to shirk it; cycled to KSHIR

annotation.surface: Long ago, a duck rode a bike round an old county.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird; it is the verb, to dodge.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Yorkshire is one of England's historic counties, now split into several.

entries.clue: Fighter, being mountain-based, occupies lower ground (8)

indicatorNotes.occupies: to occupy a place is to be inside it

blocks.note: a tor is a hill, lower ground than a mountain
an oread is a mountain nymph, a being of the mountains

annotation.surface: A soldier stationed in the mountains takes up a position lower down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a participle but is a noun: a creature. A tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a toreador is a bullfighter, one kind of fighter.

entries.clue: A favourite car in business (6)

blocks.note: the Mini, a small British car

annotation.surface: A beloved car is still going.
annotation.walkthrough: The word's older sense is meant, before it meant a lackey.
annotation.definitionFit: Archaic sense: a minion was originally a favourite of a prince or patron.
